precepts.text: Achan's covetousness brought stoning and fire on him and his whole house; one man's sin judged his family.
precepts.point: Sin brings judgment on a whole house. Achan coveted the goodly Babylonish garment, the silver, and the wedge of gold, and he and his sons and his daughters and all that he had were stoned and burned in the valley of Achor. What you do is not just about you; your sin can bring judgment on your family.

note.label: Leviticus 20: The Judgments Appointed for the Abominations

precepts.why:
The Most High set His face “against that man, and against his family.” Sin brings judgment on a whole house, and Achan is the proof.

Achan confessed: “When I saw among the spoils a goodly Babylonish garment, and two hundred shekels of silver, and a wedge of gold of fifty shekels weight, then I coveted them, and took them; and, behold, they are hid in the earth in the midst of my tent.” Joshua and all Israel took Achan “and the silver, and the garment, and the wedge of gold, and his sons, and his daughters, and his oxen, and his asses, and his sheep, and his tent, and all that he had: and they brought them unto the valley of Achor.” “And all Israel stoned him with stones, and burned them with fire.”

One man’s covetousness brought stoning and fire on him and his whole house. What you do is not just about you; your sin can bring judgment on your family.

precepts.text: Achan of the tribe of Judah took of the accursed thing, and the anger of the Lord was kindled against the children of Israel.
precepts.point: All Israel stoned Achan with stones and burned him with fire in the valley of Achor, and the Lord turned from the fierceness of his anger; righteous judgment lifted the wrath and the people were able to move forward.

note.label: Deuteronomy 13: Enticers to Other Gods Put Away

precepts.why:
When a city is withdrawn to serve other gods, the law does not strike at once. First “enquire, and make search, and ask diligently”, and only “if it be truth, and the thing certain” is the city smitten with the edge of the sword and burnt with fire. Achan is the example of this kind of judgment.

“But the children of Israel committed a trespass in the accursed thing: for Achan, the son of Carmi, the son of Zabdi, the son of Zerah, of the tribe of Judah, took of the accursed thing: and the anger of the Lord was kindled against the children of Israel.” One man of the tribe of Judah took it, and one man's folly kindled the anger of the Lord against all Israel.

Wars Israel had been winning without losing a man began to be lost, and Joshua had to search and seek out who had committed the crime in Israel. That searching is the enquire, make search, and ask diligently of this law, done before anyone was judged.

precepts.text: Joshua and all Israel brought Achan and all he had to the valley of Achor and stoned them with stones; so the Lord turned from the fierceness of his anger.
precepts.point: All Israel stoned Achan with stones and burned him with fire in the valley of Achor, and the Lord turned from the fierceness of his anger; righteous judgment lifted the wrath and the people were able to move forward.

note.label: Deuteronomy 13: Enticers to Other Gods Put Away

precepts.why:
Once the thing was certain, the judgment fell the way this law lays it out. “And Joshua, and all Israel with him, took Achan the son of Zerah, and the silver, and the garment, and the wedge of gold, and his sons, and his daughters, and his oxen, and his asses, and his sheep, and his tent, and all that he had: and they brought them unto the valley of Achor.” All that he had went with him, as the city was to be destroyed utterly, “and all that is therein, and the cattle thereof”, with all the spoil gathered and burnt.

“And all Israel stoned him with stones, and burned them with fire, after they had stoned them with stones. And they raised over him a great heap of stones unto this day.” Stoned, burned with fire, and left a heap, as the city was to be “an heap for ever”.

“So the Lord turned from the fierceness of his anger.” Righteous judgment lifted the wrath, and the people were able to move forward. That is why the place was called the valley of Achor unto this day.

precepts.text: Achan took of the accursed thing, and the anger of the Lord was kindled against the children of Israel.
precepts.point: Because of that trespass Israel could not stand before their enemies but turned their backs, for they were accursed; the Lord would not be with them any more except they destroyed the accursed from among them, and Achan and his family and all that belonged to him were destroyed and burned, and a heap set upon them, because he broke the covenant.

note.label: Deuteronomy 23: Who May Enter the Congregation and the Holy Camp

precepts.why:
The warning was not kept. “But the children of Israel committed a trespass in the accursed thing: for Achan, the son of Carmi, the son of Zabdi, the son of Zerah, of the tribe of Judah, took of the accursed thing: and the anger of the Lord was kindled against the children of Israel.”

Achan the son of Carmi of the tribe of Judah took of the accursed thing, the Babylonish garment, and though one man took it, the anger of the Lord was kindled against the children of Israel. When the host went forth and one man did not keep himself from the wicked thing, the whole camp bore it. That is why the law says keep thee from every wicked thing when the host goeth forth.

precepts.text: Israel hath sinned and taken of the accursed thing; therefore they could not stand before their enemies until the accursed was destroyed from among them.
precepts.point: Because of that trespass Israel could not stand before their enemies but turned their backs, for they were accursed; the Lord would not be with them any more except they destroyed the accursed from among them, and Achan and his family and all that belonged to him were destroyed and burned, and a heap set upon them, because he broke the covenant.

note.label: Deuteronomy 23: Who May Enter the Congregation and the Holy Camp

precepts.why:
Here is what the wicked thing in the camp cost. “Israel hath sinned, and they have also transgressed my covenant which I commanded them: for they have even taken of the accursed thing, and have also stolen, and dissembled also, and they have put it even among their own stuff. Therefore the children of Israel could not stand before their enemies, but turned their backs before their enemies, because they were accursed: neither will I be with you any more, except ye destroy the accursed from among you.”

Because of that trespass Israel could not stand before their enemies but turned their backs, for they were accursed; the Lord would not be with them any more except they destroyed the accursed from among them. “There is an accursed thing in the midst of thee, O Israel: thou canst not stand before thine enemies, until ye take away the accursed thing from among you.”

Achan and his family and all that belonged to him were destroyed and burned, and a heap set upon them, because he broke the covenant. So when the host goeth forth, keep thee from every wicked thing: it is the wicked thing in the camp that turns the battle.

precepts.text: If ye walk contrary unto me, I will walk contrary unto you also in fury, and chastise you seven times for your sins.
precepts.point: Hearts melting as water is the curse for disobedience: the Most High sends a faintness into the heart, so that the mighty flee as fleeing from a sword and fall when none pursueth, like the athlete in the scary movie suddenly stumbling from sheer fear.

note.label: Joshua 7: The Accursed Thing and the Sin of Achan

precepts.why:
About three thousand men went up to Ai, “and they fled before the men of Ai.” The way Israel had been winning, they thought they could not lose; but what happened in verse 1 was about to play its part. “And if ye will not for all this hearken unto me, but walk contrary unto me; Then I will walk contrary unto you also in fury; and I, even I, will chastise you seven times for your sins.”

The Lord is the one who wins the battles and gets the victory, not us. Pick out the weakest nation on earth: no matter how strong Israel is physically, if we are not spiritually right with the Lord, he will make us lose, for this fight is not carnal. At Ai the Lord walked contrary to Israel.

precepts.text: I will send a faintness into their hearts; the sound of a shaken leaf shall chase them, and they shall flee as fleeing from a sword, and fall when none pursueth.
precepts.point: Hearts melting as water is the curse for disobedience: the Most High sends a faintness into the heart, so that the mighty flee as fleeing from a sword and fall when none pursueth, like the athlete in the scary movie suddenly stumbling from sheer fear.

note.label: Joshua 7: The Accursed Thing and the Sin of Achan

precepts.why:
“wherefore the hearts of the people melted, and became as water.” Hearts melting as water is the curse for disobedience: “And upon them that are left alive of you I will send a faintness into their hearts in the lands of their enemies; and the sound of a shaken leaf shall chase them; and they shall flee, as fleeing from a sword; and they shall fall when none pursueth.”

The Most High sends a faintness into the heart, so that the mighty flee as fleeing from a sword and fall when none pursueth, like the athlete in the scary movie suddenly stumbling from sheer fear. Thirty and six men smitten and Israel chased from before the gate by a people that were but few: that is the faintness sent.

precepts.text: For the tidings, because it cometh: every heart shall melt, all hands shall be feeble, every spirit shall faint, and all knees shall be weak as water.
precepts.point: Hearts melting as water is the curse for disobedience: the Most High sends a faintness into the heart, so that the mighty flee as fleeing from a sword and fall when none pursueth, like the athlete in the scary movie suddenly stumbling from sheer fear.

note.label: Joshua 7: The Accursed Thing and the Sin of Achan

precepts.why:
“For the tidings; because it cometh: and every heart shall melt, and all hands shall be feeble, and every spirit shall faint, and all knees shall be weak as water: behold, it cometh, and shall be brought to pass, saith the Lord God.” Every heart melting, every spirit fainting, knees weak as water: this is the Lord's doing, and he says it shall be brought to pass.

That is what the people of Israel felt after Ai, their hearts melted and became as water. The Lord controls the heart of the fight, not the sword; if we are not spiritually right with him, he will make us lose.

precepts.text: God thundereth marvellously with his voice; great things doeth he, which we cannot comprehend.
precepts.point: Neither will I be with you any more, except ye destroy the accursed from among you: what is accursed must be destroyed; that is the only way to remove it.

note.label: Joshua 7: The Accursed Thing and the Sin of Achan

precepts.why:
“Therefore the children of Israel could not stand before their enemies, but turned their backs before their enemies, because they were accursed”. The Lord was not going to let them win, and he put a mightier warring spirit on the men of Ai. However well you train with your sword and shield, the Most High controls the outcome.

“God thundereth marvellously with his voice; great things doeth he, which we cannot comprehend.” His power cannot be comprehended. Stop trying to figure the Creator out and questioning why he created what he created; you are the creation, so keep the commandments and play your role.

And notice: “Israel hath sinned”. It does not say Achan sinned; it says Israel. This walk is not selfish or individual: when you are in sin you hurt your wife, your husband, your children, the congregation, and the leadership, for we are all our brother's keeper and responsible for one another.

precepts.text: Touching the Almighty, we cannot find him out: he is excellent in power, and in judgment, and in plenty of justice.
precepts.point: Neither will I be with you any more, except ye destroy the accursed from among you: what is accursed must be destroyed; that is the only way to remove it.

note.label: Joshua 7: The Accursed Thing and the Sin of Achan

precepts.why:
“Touching the Almighty, we cannot find him out: he is excellent in power, and in judgment, and in plenty of justice: he will not afflict.” We cannot find him out; he is excellent in power and in judgment, and his justice is plenty. That is who made Israel turn their backs before Ai, and you are not going to figure him out.

His judgment here is on the whole house: they have taken of the accursed thing, and stolen, and dissembled, and put it among their own stuff; the Lord says they. As a father who finds mischief chastens all his children together when none confesses, so the Most High deals with his children as one house; we pay for one another's sins.

“neither will I be with you any more, except ye destroy the accursed from among you.” What is accursed must be destroyed; that is the only way to remove it. Keep the commandments and play your role.

precepts.text: The eyes of the Lord are in every place, beholding the evil and the good.
precepts.point: The Lord gives a dispensation of time and grace to get the mind right, to repent, pray, and fast over what we struggle with; the just man falleth seven times and riseth up again. When leadership corrects you, do not think evil of them: the Lord did not have to send leadership, he could have sent evil your way instead; correction is the warning and the mercy.

note.label: Joshua 7: The Accursed Thing and the Sin of Achan

precepts.why:
Joshua said to Achan, “hide it not from me”, because it was already not hidden from One mightier than he: we cannot hide what we do from the Lord. “The eyes of the Lord are in every place, beholding the evil and the good.” He sees everything we do.

If you are in this walk as a manpleaser, the Lord sees what you do away from the brotherhood and the sisterhood. Achan hid what he took from men, but not from the eyes that are in every place.

precepts.text: Can any hide himself in secret places that I shall not see him? saith the Lord. Do not I fill heaven and earth?
precepts.point: The Lord gives a dispensation of time and grace to get the mind right, to repent, pray, and fast over what we struggle with; the just man falleth seven times and riseth up again. When leadership corrects you, do not think evil of them: the Lord did not have to send leadership, he could have sent evil your way instead; correction is the warning and the mercy.

note.label: Joshua 7: The Accursed Thing and the Sin of Achan

precepts.why:
“Can any hide himself in secret places that I shall not see him? saith the Lord. Do not I fill heaven and earth? saith the Lord.” There is no secret place. He fills heaven and earth, so wherever Achan put what he took, the Lord was there.

That is why Joshua says give glory to the Lord God of Israel and make confession unto him: the confession is not telling the Lord something he does not know; it is giving him glory for what he already sees.

precepts.text: The eyes of the Lord are ten thousand times brighter than the sun; you cannot hide from him.
precepts.point: The Lord gives a dispensation of time and grace to get the mind right, to repent, pray, and fast over what we struggle with; the just man falleth seven times and riseth up again. When leadership corrects you, do not think evil of them: the Lord did not have to send leadership, he could have sent evil your way instead; correction is the warning and the mercy.

note.label: Joshua 7: The Accursed Thing and the Sin of Achan

precepts.why:
“Such a man only feareth the eyes of men, and knoweth not that the eyes of the Lord are ten thousand times brighter than the sun, beholding all the ways of men, and considering the most secret parts.” The manpleaser fears the eyes of men; the eyes of the Lord are ten thousand times brighter than the sun, and they consider the most secret parts. You cannot hide from him.

So make confession unto him. The Lord gives a dispensation of time and grace to get the mind right, to repent, pray, and fast over what we struggle with; the just man falleth seven times and riseth up again.

precepts.text: If ye will not do so, ye have sinned against the Lord: and be sure your sin will find you out.
precepts.point: The Lord gives a dispensation of time and grace to get the mind right, to repent, pray, and fast over what we struggle with; the just man falleth seven times and riseth up again. When leadership corrects you, do not think evil of them: the Lord did not have to send leadership, he could have sent evil your way instead; correction is the warning and the mercy.

note.label: Joshua 7: The Accursed Thing and the Sin of Achan

precepts.why:
“But if ye will not do so, behold, ye have sinned against the Lord: and be sure your sin will find you out.” Achan's sin found him out, and Joshua stood in front of him saying, “tell me now what thou hast done; hide it not from me.”

When leadership corrects you, do not think evil of them: the Lord did not have to send leadership, he could have sent evil your way instead; correction is the warning and the mercy. Your sin will find you out; the correction is the mercy that comes before the evil.

precepts.text: Thou shalt not covet thy neighbour's house, thy neighbour's wife, nor any thing that is thy neighbour's; the last commandment, last but not least.
precepts.point: To covet is to carry the spirit of jealousy and envy, and there is not a more wicked thing than a covetous man: he sets his own soul to sale, selling out his dignity and self-respect to fulfil his desires no matter what it takes.

note.label: Joshua 7: The Accursed Thing and the Sin of Achan

precepts.why:
Achan’s own words tell where the sin began: “then I coveted them, and took them”. Covetousness is the last of the ten commandments: “Thou shalt not covet thy neighbour’s house, thou shalt not covet thy neighbour’s wife, nor his manservant, nor his maidservant, nor his ox, nor his ass, nor any thing that is thy neighbour’s.” As a father saves the weightiest warning for last but not least, the Lord ends the ten with thou shalt not covet.

Achan did not even covet his neighbour’s goods. Joshua had said all the silver and gold and vessels were consecrated unto the Lord for his treasury, so Achan was not stealing from men; he was literally stealing from the Most High. To covet is to carry the spirit of jealousy and envy, and that spirit is what carried him from seeing the goodly Babylonish garment, the two hundred shekels of silver and the wedge of gold to taking them and hiding them in the earth in the midst of his tent.

precepts.text: There is not a more wicked thing than a covetous man; he sets his own soul to sale.
precepts.point: To covet is to carry the spirit of jealousy and envy, and there is not a more wicked thing than a covetous man: he sets his own soul to sale, selling out his dignity and self-respect to fulfil his desires no matter what it takes.

note.label: Joshua 7: The Accursed Thing and the Sin of Achan

precepts.why:
“There is not a more wicked thing than a covetous man: for such an one setteth his own soul to sale”. That is Achan. He saw the goodly Babylonish garment, the silver and the wedge of gold among the spoils, coveted them and took them, though they were consecrated unto the Lord for his treasury, so he was stealing from the Most High himself.

A covetous man sells out his dignity and self-respect to fulfil his desires no matter what it takes; he sets his own soul to sale. Achan sold his for a garment and some metal hid in the earth in the midst of his tent. Covetousness carries the spirit of jealousy and envy, and the Lord counted it weighty enough to close the ten commandments with it.

precepts.text: My people are destroyed for lack of knowledge; seeing thou hast forgotten the law of thy God, I will also forget thy children.
precepts.point: They raised over him a great heap of stones unto this day, and the Lord turned from the fierceness of his anger; wherefore the name of that place was called the valley of Achor unto this day.

note.label: Joshua 7: The Accursed Thing and the Sin of Achan

precepts.why:
“My people are destroyed for lack of knowledge: because thou hast rejected knowledge, I will also reject thee”. We quote that often, but the end of the verse we seldom quote says, “seeing thou hast forgotten the law of thy God, I will also forget thy children.”

That is why the scripture says all Israel “burned them with fire, after they had stoned them with stones”: them, because his household went with him. Achan’s sons and daughters did not steal the garment, the silver or the wedge of gold, yet because he lacked knowledge and understanding they paid for the covetous spirit he carried. His selfish, individual spirit never weighed what his family would pay; he was the reason men died in that battle and the nation was nearly overtaken.

The Lord hits where it hurts. Your sin reaches your children, your wife, your husband, your brothers and sisters. Reject knowledge and the Lord will reject thee, and he will forget thy children too.

precepts.text: It is a fearful thing to fall into the hands of the living God.
precepts.point: They raised over him a great heap of stones unto this day, and the Lord turned from the fierceness of his anger; wherefore the name of that place was called the valley of Achor unto this day.

note.label: Joshua 7: The Accursed Thing and the Sin of Achan

precepts.why:
“It is a fearful thing to fall into the hands of the living God.” That is where Achan fell, and unfortunately his sons and daughters and all he had with him. The Lord revealed what was hid in the earth in the midst of his tent, and the scripture cannot be broken: as Jericho was made a curse, so the one who took of it. All Israel stoned him, burned them with fire, and raised over him a great heap of stones unto this day.

Some of our people in the islands and elsewhere still ignorantly carry out such public executions to this day. We do not condone it, for we are not under the law of sacrifice now but under grace, and the judgment is of the Lord. But the fear should stay with us: Achan, an Israelite of Judah, lacked faith and was put to death, while Rahab the Canaanite harlot was saved alive for her faith. We must have the fear of the Lord in our hearts.

precepts.text: Moab and Seir do say, Behold, the house of Judah is like unto all the heathen; disobedience makes the Lord liken Israel unto the heathen.
precepts.point: They raised over him a great heap of stones unto this day, and the Lord turned from the fierceness of his anger; wherefore the name of that place was called the valley of Achor unto this day.

note.label: Joshua 7: The Accursed Thing and the Sin of Achan

precepts.why:
“Because that Moab and Seir do say, Behold, the house of Judah is like unto all the heathen”. Achan was of Judah, and he was stoned and burned in the valley of Achor like the accursed thing he took. When Israel will not obey his voice, the Lord likens the house of Judah unto all the heathen.

Consider the contrast that closes these chapters: Achan the Israelite of Judah lacked faith and was put to death, while Rahab the Canaanite harlot was saved alive for her faith. Disobedience makes the Lord treat Israel like the heathen, so we must have the fear of the Lord in our hearts.

precepts.text: Achan of the tribe of Judah took of the accursed thing, and the anger of the Lord was kindled against all the children of Israel.
precepts.point: They cited the proof from their own history: did not Achan the son of Zerah commit a trespass in the accursed thing, and wrath fell on all the congregation of Israel, and that man perished not alone in his iniquity. One man trespassed and the whole nation felt it.

note.label: Joshua 22: The Altar of Witness

precepts.why:
The children of Israel cite the proof from their own history: “Did not Achan the son of Zerah commit a trespass in the accursed thing, and wrath fell on all the congregation of Israel?” “But the children of Israel committed a trespass in the accursed thing: for Achan, the son of Carmi, the son of Zabdi, the son of Zerah, of the tribe of Judah, took of the accursed thing: and the anger of the Lord was kindled against the children of Israel.”

One man of the tribe of Judah took of the accursed thing, and the anger of the Lord was kindled against all the children of Israel. One man trespassed and the whole nation felt it. That is why they came to the two and a half tribes over an altar: if it was rebellion, it would not stay on the other side Jordan.

precepts.text: He that is taken with the accursed thing shall be burnt with fire, he and all that he hath, because he hath transgressed the covenant of the Lord.
precepts.point: They cited the proof from their own history: did not Achan the son of Zerah commit a trespass in the accursed thing, and wrath fell on all the congregation of Israel, and that man perished not alone in his iniquity. One man trespassed and the whole nation felt it.

note.label: Joshua 22: The Altar of Witness

precepts.why:
“and that man perished not alone in his iniquity.” “And it shall be, that he that is taken with the accursed thing shall be burnt with fire, he and all that he hath: because he hath transgressed the covenant of the Lord, and because he hath wrought folly in Israel.”

Achan was burnt with fire, he and all that he had, for transgressing the covenant of the Lord. Wrath fell on the congregation, and the man did not perish alone. So the offer stands: if your land be unclean, come over and take possession among us, close by where we can keep an eye on you; only rebel not against the Lord, nor build an altar beside the altar of the Lord our God.

precepts.point: Faithful are the wounds of a friend, but the kisses of an enemy are deceitful.

note.label: Proverbs 27: Boast Not of Tomorrow

precepts.why:
“Open rebuke is better than secret love.” Many of us leaving the Christian church were shocked to see men stood up and rebuked openly, but that is the law, and the law does it so that people may learn to fear the Most High.

Achan in Joshua 7 is the pattern. His sin was found out before all Israel, and he, with his family and his substance, was stoned and burned before all. Nothing about it was done in secret; the whole camp saw the rebuke and the judgment, so the whole camp learned to fear.

That open rebuke is a faithful wound from a friend. Secret love that lets a man go on in his sin is the kiss of an enemy, and the kisses of an enemy are deceitful.

moments.label: Dark Places of the Heart: the Hidden Cost of Sin

points: Israel committed a trespass in the accursed thing: Achan of the tribe of Judah took what Moses commanded be burned, and the anger of the Lord was kindled against all Israel.

note.label: Dark Places of the Heart: the Hidden Cost of Sin

points: The spies said Ai was few and only two or three thousand men needed to go up. They fled, and thirty-six men died, because of one man's secret sin. There is always that one. It only takes one bad apple.

note.label: Dark Places of the Heart: the Hidden Cost of Sin

points: The Lord told Joshua that Israel had sinned, stolen and dissembled, and therefore could not stand before their enemies. No man saw Achan, but God did. Joshua investigated tribe by tribe, family by family, man by man, until Achan was taken, and told him to give glory to God and confess.

note.label: Dark Places of the Heart: the Hidden Cost of Sin

points: In the middle of a war this man found time to covet a Babylonish garment, silver and gold and bury them in his tent. Some brothers today want to give up rank in the middle of warfare because they do not understand it.

note.label: Dark Places of the Heart: the Hidden Cost of Sin

points: Joshua took Achan with his sons, daughters, animals and tent to the valley of Achor, because the household had to have known and said nothing. Silence is agreement. Israel stoned and burned them and raised a heap of stones. Secret sin cost thirty-six men their lives and wiped out a whole family.

note.label: Dark Places of the Heart: the Hidden Cost of Sin

points: Why hast thou troubled us? Some of you trouble the camp with your foolishness and hinder the work; you are taking a seat a brother or sister out there could use. The leaders cannot stone anyone, but there is a God who brings judgment, and some would prefer the stones to what he has for them.

note.label: Dark Places of the Heart: the Hidden Cost of Sin

points: Who committed the trespass? Many will answer Achan, but read the first sentence: the children of Israel committed a trespass in the accursed thing. Achan the son of Carmi, the son of Zabdi, the son of Zerah, of the tribe of Judah, took of the accursed thing, and the anger of the Lord was kindled against all the children of Israel.

Your individual sins can hurt the rest of the nation. You can be the hindrance to why your camp is not growing, why your family, your marriage, or your children have issues, when you have a spirit on you that you know about and keep secret, not praying, not fasting, not seeking counsel. That is the spirit of Achan, and the children of Israel pay for it; we are supposed to be one mind, one body, one spirit.

note.label: Joshua 7: The Accursed Thing and the Sin of Achan

points: The men who viewed Ai came back confident: let not all the people go up, but about two or three thousand men, for they are but few. The way Israel had been winning, they thought they could not lose; but what happened in verse 1 was about to play its part.

note.label: Joshua 7: The Accursed Thing and the Sin of Achan

points: About three thousand went up, and they fled before the men of Ai, who smote about thirty and six men and chased them from before the gate; the hearts of the people melted and became as water.

Hearts melting as water is the curse for disobedience: the Most High sends a faintness into the heart, so that the mighty flee as fleeing from a sword and fall when none pursueth, like the athlete in the scary movie suddenly stumbling from sheer fear.

note.label: Joshua 7: The Accursed Thing and the Sin of Achan

points: Joshua rent his clothes and fell to the earth upon his face before the ark until the eventide, he and the elders of Israel, and put dust upon their heads, grieving over the war just lost and the men that died.

note.label: Joshua 7: The Accursed Thing and the Sin of Achan

points: Israel turning their backs means they were fleeing, retreating, defeated. Joshua understood what the nations do when they see Israel take a loss: the Canaanites would hear of it, environ us round, surround us, capitalize while we are down, and cut off our name from the earth.
And what wilt thou do unto thy great name? If Israel is cut off, who will be there to praise the Most High?

note.label: Joshua 7: The Accursed Thing and the Sin of Achan

points: The Lord said, Get thee up; wherefore liest thou upon thy face? Israel hath sinned. It does not say Achan sinned; it says Israel. This walk is not selfish or individual: when you are in sin you hurt your wife, your husband, your children, the congregation, and the leadership, for we are all our brother's keeper and responsible for one another.

note.label: Joshua 7: The Accursed Thing and the Sin of Achan

points: They have taken of the accursed thing, and stolen, and dissembled, and put it among their own stuff: the Lord says they. As a father who finds mischief chastens all his children together when none confesses, so the Most High deals with his children as one house; we pay for one another's sins.

note.label: Joshua 7: The Accursed Thing and the Sin of Achan

points: Therefore the children of Israel could not stand before their enemies: the Lord was not going to let them win, and he put a mightier warring spirit on the men of Ai. However well you train with your sword and shield, the Most High controls the outcome.
Neither will I be with you any more, except ye destroy the accursed from among you: what is accursed must be destroyed; that is the only way to remove it.

note.label: Joshua 7: The Accursed Thing and the Sin of Achan

points: Up, sanctify the people against tomorrow: there is an accursed thing in the midst of thee, O Israel; thou canst not stand before thine enemies until ye take away the accursed thing from among you.

note.label: Joshua 7: The Accursed Thing and the Sin of Achan

points: The search would narrow by the Lord's own taking: tribe, then family, then household, then man by man; and he that is taken with the accursed thing shall be burnt with fire, he and all that he hath.

The folly was wrought against a plain commandment: Joshua had already charged them in Joshua 6:18-19 to keep from the accursed thing lest they trouble the camp, and adjured them in Joshua 6:26; the transgressor troubled the camp, the army and congregation of Israel.

note.label: Joshua 7: The Accursed Thing and the Sin of Achan

points: Joshua rose up early and brought Israel by their tribes, and the tribe of Judah was taken; then the family of the Zarhites, then the household of Zabdi man by man, and Achan the son of Carmi, the son of Zabdi, the son of Zerah, of the tribe of Judah, was taken.

note.label: Joshua 7: The Accursed Thing and the Sin of Achan

points: My son, give, I pray thee, glory to the Lord God of Israel, and make confession unto him; and tell me now what thou hast done; hide it not from me. Joshua said hide it not from me because it was already not hidden from One mightier than he: we cannot hide what we do from the Lord.

The eyes of the Lord are in every place, beholding the evil and the good; he sees everything we do. If you are in this walk as a manpleaser, the Lord sees what you do away from the brotherhood and the sisterhood.

The Lord gives a dispensation of time and grace to get the mind right, to repent, pray, and fast over what we struggle with; the just man falleth seven times and riseth up again. When leadership corrects you, do not think evil of them: the Lord did not have to send leadership, he could have sent evil your way instead; correction is the warning and the mercy.

note.label: Joshua 7: The Accursed Thing and the Sin of Achan

points: Joshua had said all the silver and gold and vessels were consecrated unto the Lord for his treasury, so Achan was not stealing from men; he was literally stealing from the Most High.

note.label: Joshua 7: The Accursed Thing and the Sin of Achan

points: Achan confessed: indeed I have sinned against the Lord God of Israel. He saw among the spoils a goodly Babylonish garment, two hundred shekels of silver, and a wedge of gold of fifty shekels weight; he coveted them, took them, and hid them in the earth in the midst of his tent.

note.label: Joshua 7: The Accursed Thing and the Sin of Achan

points: Joshua sent messengers, and they ran unto the tent, and behold, it was hid in his tent, and the silver under it; they laid it all out before the Lord with the whole congregation present. The Lord revealed it, and the scripture cannot be broken: as Jericho was made a curse, so the one who took of it.

note.label: Joshua 7: The Accursed Thing and the Sin of Achan

points: Consider the contrast that closes these chapters: Achan, an Israelite of Judah, lacked faith and was put to death, while Rahab the Canaanite harlot was saved alive for her faith. When Israel will not obey his voice, the Lord likens the house of Judah unto all the heathen; so we must have the fear of the Lord in our hearts.

note.label: Joshua 7: The Accursed Thing and the Sin of Achan

points: Joshua and all Israel took Achan, the silver, the garment, the wedge of gold, and his sons, and his daughters, and his oxen, asses, sheep, tent, and all that he had, unto the valley of Achor. His sons and daughters did not steal it, yet because he lacked knowledge and understanding they paid for the covetous spirit he carried.

It is a fearful thing to fall into the hands of the living God, and that is where Achan fell, and unfortunately his sons and daughters and all he had with him. Some of our people in the islands and elsewhere still ignorantly carry out such public executions to this day; we do not condone it, for we are not under the law of sacrifice now but under grace, and the judgment is of the Lord.

note.label: Joshua 7: The Accursed Thing and the Sin of Achan

points: Why hast thou troubled us? the Lord shall trouble thee this day. Achan was the reason men died in that battle and the nation was nearly overtaken; his selfish, individual spirit never weighed what his family would pay.

All Israel stoned him with stones, and burned them with fire, after they had stoned them with stones: them, because his household went with him. My people are destroyed for lack of knowledge: reject knowledge and the Lord will reject thee, and the end of Hosea 4:6 that we seldom quote says, I will also forget thy children. The Lord hits where it hurts, and your sin reaches your children, your wife, your husband, your brothers and sisters.

note.label: Joshua 7: The Accursed Thing and the Sin of Achan

points: They raised over him a great heap of stones unto this day, and the Lord turned from the fierceness of his anger; wherefore the name of that place was called the valley of Achor unto this day.

note.label: Joshua 7: The Accursed Thing and the Sin of Achan
